newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Friday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Friday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Friday:

Spokesman Patrick Child briefed on Sunday night and Monday's ECOFIN Council. He said discussions would focus on euro coins, Ireland's convergence programme and employment in preparation for the Amsterdam European Council.
Child said Commissioner Mario Monti would sign a customs cooperation agreement with Switzerland at 1100/0900 GMT on Monday.
Spokesman Nikolaus van der Pas said there would be a meeting of the permanent representatives to the IGC on Monday and Tuesday.
Van der Pas also reminded that the Commission would meet on Tuesday in Strasbourg.

In answer to a question about a unilateral British declaration concerning proposed measures to restrict imports of beef from other member states, spokesman Gerry Kiely said there was no mention, in the British declaration, of a ban on beef from any other country.
Asked to react to the EP vote on two draft regulations to go in the package of the stability growth pact, voted on May 28, Child said the ECOFIN Ministers would take them into account on Monday.

Child also said the member states public investments expenditure, as reported by the Commission, would be taken into consideration by the Council when deciding which states would join the EMU but would not be deduced from the public deficit.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/97/473: EU and Guatemala: signing of the joint declaration on the implementation of the EU contribution to the peace process.
- IP/97/496: Commission approves Comapgnie de Suez/Lyonnaise des Eaux merger.
- IP/97/497: Commission approves a news framework to support the market for telecommunications terminals.
- IP/97/498: Commission clears acquisition by TYCO of ADT in the fire and security alarm sector.
- Eurostat - Economy and finance: ECU-EMS information & Central Banks interest rates No 1997-4/5.
